skill.name: mermaid-diagrams
skill.description: Create and refine Mermaid diagrams for software architecture, process flows, sequence interactions, class models, entity relationships, C4 views, and project timelines.
skill.summary: Guides AI agents through Mermaid syntax for clear software and documentation diagrams.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Mermaid documentation and example syntax. Terms such as System, Network, Database, and Email are diagram labels, URLs are documentation examples, and backticks are Markdown formatting. No executable scripts, data exfiltration intent, prompt injection, or unsafe automation was found.

static_findings.snippet: Transform complex technical concepts into clear, maintainable diagrams that can be version-controlle
Mermaid syntax is intuitive and follows a consistent pattern across all diagram types:
- **VS Code** - Preview with Markdown Mermaid extension
- **Export** - PNG, SVG, PDF via Mermaid Live or CLI
7. **Validate syntax** - Test in Mermaid Live before committing
- **Export for presentations** - Use Mermaid Live or CLI for high-res exports
- **[Mermaid Live Editor](https://mermaid.live)** - Interactive editor with instant preview and expo
- **VS Code Extension** - "Markdown Preview Mermaid Support" for live preview
8. **Use enum/check constraints** - Enforce valid values at database level
3. **Comment Extensively** - Use `%%` comments to explain complex relationships
5. **Version Control** - Store `.mmd` files alongside code for easy updates
- `layout: elk` - Advanced layout for complex diagrams (requires integration)
- Mermaid CLI - `npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` then `mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png`
- [Mermaid Live Editor](https://mermaid.live) - Online editor with PNG/SVG export
description: Comprehensive guide for creating software diagrams using Mermaid syntax. Use when users
Create professional software diagrams using Mermaid's text-based syntax. Mermaid renders diagrams fr
All Mermaid diagrams follow this pattern:
- VS Code - With Markdown Mermaid extension
- [Mermaid Live Editor](https://mermaid.live) - Online editor with PNG/SVG export
- Mermaid CLI - `npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` then `mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png`
- **Breaking characters** - Avoid `{}` in comments, use proper escape sequences for special characte
- **Syntax errors** - Misspellings break diagrams; validate syntax in Mermaid Live

content.user_title: Create Mermaid Diagrams for Software Documentation
content.value_statement: Teams often need clear diagrams that stay close to code and documentation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Mermaid syntax for maintainable visual models.
actual_capabilities: Selects suitable Mermaid diagram types for architecture, workflow, data, and interaction needs.
Provides syntax guidance for class diagrams, sequence diagrams, flowcharts, ERDs, and C4 diagrams.
Explains Mermaid relationships, participants, node shapes, cardinality, containers, components, and styling options.
Supports diagram refinement with titles, notes, comments, labels, themes, and layout choices.
Offers export guidance for Mermaid Live Editor, Mermaid CLI, Docker, and Markdown rendering tools.
limitations: It does not render diagrams inside the skill by itself.
It cannot verify Mermaid output unless a compatible renderer or editor is available.
Complex diagrams may still need manual layout adjustments after generation.
Some advanced Mermaid options depend on the renderer version used by the target platform.

use_cases.title: Document Service Architecture
use_cases.description: Create C4 diagrams that show systems, containers, components, users, and external services.

use_cases.title: Explain Application Flows
use_cases.description: Build sequence diagrams and flowcharts for API calls, user journeys, and business processes.

use_cases.title: Model Data Structures
use_cases.description: Create ERD and class diagrams for database schemas, domain models, and object relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Flowchart
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple process diagram.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid flowchart for this process: [describe the steps]. Use clear labels and one decision point.

prompt_templates.title: Map an API Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for request and response interactions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid sequence diagram for this API flow: [describe actors, calls, responses, and error cases].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Data Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for schema and relationship planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid ERD for this domain: [describe entities, attributes, keys, and relationships]. Include cardinality.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a C4 Architecture View
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for layered system documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Mermaid C4 context, container, and component views for this system: [describe users, services, stores, and dependencies].

output_examples.input: A login flow with a user, web app, API, identity provider, and database.
output_examples.output: A sequence diagram showing authentication, token creation, user lookup, success response, and invalid credential handling.

output_examples.input: An order management database with customers, orders, products, and line items.
output_examples.output: An ERD that defines entities, primary keys, foreign keys, and one-to-many relationships between orders and line items.

output_examples.input: A microservice platform with web, API, queue, notification, payment, and database components.
output_examples.output: A C4 container diagram showing users, applications, data stores, external systems, and communication protocols.

best_practices: Start with the smallest diagram that answers the documentation question.
Use clear labels, titles, and comments so diagrams remain useful during code review.
Keep Mermaid source near related documentation or code so updates are easy to review.
anti_patterns: Do not combine every system detail into one large diagram.
Do not use vague node names when real service, entity, or actor names are known.
Do not rely on renderer-specific features without checking the target platform.

faq.question: Can this skill create Mermaid syntax for common diagram types?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, ERDs, C4 diagrams, state diagrams, and timeline-style diagrams.

faq.question: Does this skill render the final image?
faq.answer: No. It provides Mermaid text and export guidance. Rendering depends on tools such as GitHub, Mermaid Live Editor, or Mermaid CLI.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it useful for architecture reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes C4 guidance for context, container, and component diagrams used in architecture documentation.

faq.question: Can it help with database schema documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes ERD guidance for entities, keys, attributes, relationships, and cardinality.

faq.question: What should I provide for the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the purpose, audience, key entities, main steps, relationships, and any platform where the diagram will be rendered.
